newsitem.title: UK: P&U Q2 EPS drop worse than expected.
newsitem.headline: P&U Q2 EPS drop worse than expected.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said on Tuesday its second-quarter earnings per share dropped to $0.34, down from $0.51 a year before and $0.37 in the first quarter.

The struggling company, which issued its fourth profits warning since merger earlier this month, said sales fell four percent to $1.703 billion, in stark contrast to surging sales enjoyed by most of its rivals.

New president and chief executive officer Fred Hassan said the company had not changed its view "that negative sales and earnings trends seen in the first half are likely to continue through 1997, especially as we will not repeat last year's second-half trade inventory build-ups."
The EPS figure failed to meet even the sharply pared-down analysts' forecasts of around $0.36 per share. Before the latest warning, expectations had been as high as $0.50.

Hassan said the continued strength of the dollar helped reduce sales by six percent in the second quarter. Without this, sales would have been up by 2 percent overall. Generic competition is also eating into sales.
"The loss in sales and especially the loss in profits from our older products is exceeding the addition of sales and profits from our newer products," said Hassan.
He added that 1997 was "the year of repair; 1998 should be a turnaround year."
